title: Source dimension bound from dimensions of the target and fibres
statement: Let $f:X\to Y$ be a locally finite type morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-finite-type-morphism], with $Y$ locally Noetherian [pqf-def-locnoeth]. For any $d\in\{ -\infty,0,1,\ldots,\infty\}$ such that every topological fibre $f^{-1}(y)$ has dimension at most $d$ [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension], one has $\dim X\leq\dim Y+d$, with the standard addition on $\operatorname{WithBot}(\mathbb N\cup\{\infty\})$ (bottom is absorbing). No quasi-compactness or irreducibility hypothesis is imposed.

source.place: Tag 00OM, lemma-dimension-base-fibre-total; existing Lean proof in WeilConjectures/AlgebraicGeometry/FiberDimension.lean, theorems Scheme.Hom.coheight_le_coheight_add_topologicalKrullDim and Scheme.Hom.topologicalKrullDim_le_add

proof.text: Use the existing proved source-library theorem attached to this node. At any x, choose affine neighbourhoods U of x and V of f(x) with U mapping into V. Local Noetherianity of Y and local finite type make both affine rings Noetherian. The height inequality for a prime lying over a prime bounds the codimension of x by the codimension of f(x) plus the dimension of the local fibre ring. Primes below the corresponding fibre prime give a chain of points in the topological fibre, so that local fibre ring dimension is bounded by dim f inverse of f(x), hence by d. The codimension of f(x) is at most dim Y. Since a scheme is sober, dim X is the supremum of its point codimensions; taking this supremum proves dim X at most dim Y plus d. The empty case is the supremum of the empty family, namely bottom. This attaches an existing fully proved declaration; it adds no Lean obligation.
